articles.title: Getting Started with MLOps: ML models and Amazon Sagemaker
articles.excerpt: A machine learning model is more than just training an algorithm on data. Once a model is trained, how do we deploy it, make predictions, monitor its performance, and update it when needed? This is wh…
articles.body: A machine learning model is more than just training an algorithm on data. Once a model is trained, how do we deploy it, make predictions, monitor its performance, and update it when needed? This is where MLOps comes in: Machine Learning: Building and training models using data. MLOps: Managing the ML lifecycle, from expermientation and training to deployment and monitoring Amazon Sagemaker: Amazon Sagemaker is an AWS machine learning service that provides tools and infrastructure to build, train, deploy, and manage ML models A simple way to understand the workflow: Data -> Model training -> Model Evaluation -> Deployment -> Monitoring I am starting by exploring the fundamental of MLOps and how Amazon Sagemaker helps take ML models from experimentation to production.

articles.title: Why Passkeys Break in Production: WebAuthn AuthData, CBOR, and the signCount Trap
articles.excerpt: Everyone pitching passkeys makes it sound effortless: "It's just public key cryptography! No more password resets, no phishing, instant biometrics!" Then you roll it out to 50,000 real-world users in…
articles.body: Everyone pitching passkeys makes it sound effortless: "It's just public key cryptography! No more password resets, no phishing, instant biometrics!" Then you roll it out to 50,000 real-world users in production, and your exception trackers immediately light up with mysterious verification failures: WebAuthnVerificationError: Signature counter regression detected Invalid CBOR COSE key encoding: unexpected map key type Mismatched clientDataJSON challenge hash Why does WebAuthn break so easily when moving from localhost demos to real production devices? Because passkeys synced via Apple iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager violate assumptions that backend developers have relied on for a decade with physical security keys.
articles.author: Jason Y. (dev_in_the_fog)

articles.title: Our agent's self-description failed its own verification. That's the point.
articles.excerpt: Our agent's self-description failed its own verification. That's the point. Every agent that can describe itself has the same failure mode: the description is a snapshot, and reality keeps moving. You…
articles.body: Our agent's self-description failed its own verification. That's the point. Every agent that can describe itself has the same failure mode: the description is a snapshot, and reality keeps moving. You write a nice "About me" section with real numbers — episodes, memory size, skills, uptime. You commit it. Twenty-four hours later it is confidently wrong. Nothing crashed, nothing alerted. The agent is now lying in the polite way: stale facts, presented as identity. OpenAmer is an open-source agent that runs on a Windows laptop ( github.com/openamer/openamer , Apache-2.0, CPU-only). It ships a small CLI surface that treats its own self-description as a thing to be checked , not written once: usage: openamer identity [-h] {show,refresh,verify,facts,genesis} ...

articles.title: Linkerd vs Istio: Choosing the Right Service Mesh
articles.excerpt: A platform team I worked with burned six weeks rolling Istio across an 800-pod cluster, then discovered their on-call rotation couldn't debug a broken request path without three istioctl proxy-config…
articles.body: A platform team I worked with burned six weeks rolling Istio across an 800-pod cluster, then discovered their on-call rotation couldn't debug a broken request path without three istioctl proxy-config incantations and a Kiali dashboard nobody had learned to read. The mesh worked. The humans didn't. They ripped it out and installed Linkerd in an afternoon. That story isn't an argument that Istio is bad. It's an argument that the mesh decision is a team decision, not a feature decision. The wrong mesh at the wrong scale is technical debt you pay for in 3 AM pages. This guide is for platform engineers, SREs, and DevOps leads running Kubernetes somewhere between 10 and 5,000 pods.

articles.title: Anyone can ship a ModHeader replacement with AI now. That's the scary part.
articles.excerpt: Quick recap if you missed it. In July, Google and Microsoft pulled ModHeader, the header-editing extension with 1.6 million installs, after researchers found a browsing-history collector hiding in the…
articles.body: Quick recap if you missed it. In July, Google and Microsoft pulled ModHeader, the header-editing extension with 1.6 million installs, after researchers found a browsing-history collector hiding in the code (it was switched off). The switch was an empty array that any routine update could have filled. Your browser would have just installed it one afternoon like any other version bump. Within a few weeks, at least six "safe alternatives" showed up. Different names, same blog post. I know, because I just shipped one too. Here's what nobody in that pile is saying out loud: in 2026, building something like a header extension is almost free (assuming you know how to manage your tokens). I'd love to tell you mine took months of craftsmanship.

articles.title: What caused a mysterious atmospheric explosion in Siberia in 1908?
articles.excerpt: Fire erupted in the morning skies over Siberia on June 30, 1908, as an atmospheric explosion occurred that remains unmatched by any similar event in modern history.
articles.body: Fire erupted in the morning skies over Siberia on June 30, 1908, as an atmospheric explosion occurred that remains unmatched by any similar event in modern history. That day, at approximately 7:15 a.m. local time, observers in Siberia's remote Tunguska region became witnesses to the entry of a brilliant fireball into Earth's atmosphere , trailing smoke across the dawn sky and culminating in a flash brighter than the sun itself. Within seconds, the explosion and resulting shock waves that followed reportedly knocked some members of the nearby Indigenous Evenki population off their feet, and caused damage to dwellings and livestock, while seismic instruments hundreds of miles away logged tremors caused by the blast.

articles.title: UAE unveils lander for bold 7-asteroid mission set to launch in 2028 (photos)
articles.excerpt: In March 2028, the UAE is set to launch an ambitious mission to the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter that will culminate with a landing attempt on a mysteriously reddish space rock.
articles.body: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has moved a step closer to launching its second-ever interplanetary mission — an ambitious, eight-year exploration of seven asteroids between Mars and Jupiter that will culminate with a landing on the mysteriously red asteroid 269 Justitia. The mission team unveiled a half-scale model of the homegrown probe that will make that landing during an Oct. 1 press conference in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the UAE. The autonomous craft will ride attached to the main spacecraft MBR Explorer , named after Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum, the ruler of Dubai and the UAE's prime minister.

articles.title: Mars may be a hellhole, but the moon is not far behind
articles.excerpt: Welcome to the second space race. You can be forgiven for experiencing déjà vu. Last time, it was the Soviet Union and the United States vying to be the first to plant some flags. Now it’s a sprint to…
articles.body: Welcome to the second space race. You can be forgiven for experiencing déjà vu. Last time, it was the Soviet Union and the United States vying to be the first to plant some flags. Now it’s a sprint to the lunar surface between America and China—alongside a host of varyingly friendly and rival nations—plus a cornucopia of private spaceflight companies. And this time it looks like they’re getting ready to set up camp. There will be, the contenders say, bases on the moon, permanently inhabited castles under the stars. The notion of a moon base, fanciful as it might sound, isn’t new. But this year, under the leadership of Administrator Jared Isaacman, NASA has been flooding the zone with bold announcements .
